# Tokyo Family Trip at a Glance

A 5-day plan for **2 adults + 1 child (age 8)** in Tokyo from **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-14**, keeping the trip around **USD 3,500 total excluding international flights**. I’ve prioritized **3-star or better hotels near subway access**, **kid-friendly pacing**, and **moderate walking under 10,000 steps/day when possible**.

## Best Hotel Bases Near Subway Access

| Hotel Area | Why it works for families | Typical nightly range | Best for |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **Ueno / Okachimachi** | Easy subway/JR access, parks, museums, simple food options | **USD 140–230** | First-time visitors, lower transit stress |
| **Shinjuku** | Many lines, lots of hotels, easy day-trip departures | **USD 170–280** | Convenience and late-evening flexibility |
| **Asakusa** | Walkable sightseeing area, good value, family-friendly atmosphere | **USD 130–220** | Quieter base with classic Tokyo sights |
| **Tokyo Station / Nihonbashi** | Excellent transit links, efficient for citywide movement | **USD 200–320** | Best logistics, but usually pricier |
| **Shibuya** | Strong subway access, central for modern attractions | **USD 190–310** | Teens/older kids, central city energy |

## 5-Day Tokyo Family Itinerary with Estimated Costs

| Day | Focus | Main plan | Low-cost food option | Est. cost (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| **Day 1 — Apr 10** | Arrival + easy Asakusa | Check in, Senso-ji, Nakamise stroll, Sumida riverside, early night | **Convenience-store bento + onigiri** | **$190** |
| **Day 2 — Apr 11** | Ueno parks + museums | Ueno Park, National Museum or Zoo, Ameyoko, relaxed dinner | **Ramen set lunch** | **$230** |
| **Day 3 — Apr 12** | Odaiba family day | teamLab Planets or Miraikan, seaside promenade, shopping mall breaks | **Food court curry rice** | **$260** |
| **Day 4 — Apr 13** | Shibuya / Harajuku / Meiji area | Meiji Jingu, Yoyogi Park, Shibuya crossing, kid-friendly café stop | **Udon or soba lunch** | **$240** |
| **Day 5 — Apr 14** | Disney-style finale or flexible city day | Tokyo Skytree + Solamachi, aquarium option, souvenir time, departure prep | **Supermarket sushi tray** | **$220** |

## Day-by-Day Family Plan

### Day 1: Easy Arrival in Asakusa
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, rest, and keep the first day light.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Senso-ji** and browse **Nakamise Shopping Street**; good for a stroller or slow walk.
- **Evening:** Short riverside walk near Sumida; early dinner and sleep.
- **Food:** Convenience-store bento, onigiri, yogurt, fruit.
- **Walking target:** About **5,000–7,000 steps**.
- **Estimated cost:** **$190**.

### Day 2: Ueno Parks and Museums
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Spend time in **Ueno Park**; open space helps kids recover from travel.
Media: Alt=Morning:** Spend time in **Ueno Park**; open space helps kids recover from travel, Tokyo, Japan
- **Afternoon:** Choose **Tokyo National Museum** for culture or **Ueno Zoo** for a child-friendly alternative.
- **Evening:** Browse **Ameyoko** and keep dinner simple near the hotel.
- **Food:** Ramen lunch or set meal around Ueno.
- **Walking target:** About **7,000–9,500 steps**.
- **Estimated cost:** **$230**.

### Day 3: Odaiba Indoor-Outdoor Balance
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- **Morning:** Head to **teamLab Planets** or **Miraikan** depending on ticket availability and your child’s interest.
- **Afternoon:** Walk the waterfront, use mall breaks, and keep the pace relaxed.
- **Evening:** Return early; Odaiba works well for a low-stress family day.
- **Food:** Food-court curry rice or a family set meal.
- **Walking target:** About **6,000–8,500 steps**.
- **Estimated cost:** **$260**.

### Day 4: Shibuya, Harajuku, and Meiji Shrine
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Meiji Jingu** and nearby **Yoyogi Park** for a calmer start.
Media: Alt=Morning:** Visit **Meiji Jingu** and nearby **Yoyogi Park** for a calmer start, Tokyo, Japan
- **Afternoon:** See **Shibuya Crossing**, then do a short shopping stop or café break.
- **Evening:** Keep dinner near Shibuya or back at the hotel area.
- **Food:** Udon or soba lunch, usually fast and budget-friendly.
- **Walking target:** About **7,000–9,500 steps**.
- **Estimated cost:** **$240**.

### Day 5: Skytree Finale and Departure Buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Tokyo Skytree** and the **Solamachi** complex for final sightseeing and souvenirs.
- **Afternoon:** Optional **Sumida Aquarium** if your child wants one last indoor activity.
- **Evening:** Pack, transfer, and leave a comfortable buffer for departure logistics.
- **Food:** Supermarket sushi tray or deli meal.
- **Walking target:** About **5,000–8,000 steps**.
- **Estimated cost:** **$220**.

## Budget Fit for the Whole Trip

| Cost bucket | Estimated total |
|---|---:|
| Hotel, 4 nights | **$700–1,100** |
| Local transport | **$120–180** |
| Attractions and tickets | **$350–650** |
| Food and drinks | **$600–850** |
| Local extras / souvenirs | **$150–300** |
| **Trip total** | **$1,920–3,080** |

This keeps you **within the $3,500 cap** with room for a nicer hotel, extra snacks, or one premium attraction.

## Best Hotel Options to Target

### 1) Ueno area family hotel
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Strong value for a 3-star or better stay.
- Close to subway/JR lines and Ueno Park.
- Best if you want the easiest balance of price and access.

### 2) Asakusa hotel near Asakusa Station
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Good for a calmer family base.
- Easy access to classic sightseeing and affordable food.
- Often the best fit for a child-friendly first trip.

### 3) Shinjuku hotel near a subway stop
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Best for transport flexibility.
- Good if you want easy movement across the city.
- Usually costs more, but can still fit your budget.
